InfiniSplat v1 background + opaque laptop/cup surfaces, personal technical evaluation.
Source: zju3dv/InfiniSplat, commit be49948e92f828054d98103cd98578fada8ec728 (PRL).
Weights: PLUS-WAVE/InfiniSplat, revision 455dc3f21f3b2ddba37df65443112882fc6016d2 (Apache 2.0).
Upstream DINOv3 and Depth Pro terms remain applicable.
Spark viewer is reused from ../gs-lab/vendor/, see its bundled license.
The unchanged previous completion remains available at ../occlusion-lab/index.html.
The original InfiniSplat result remains available at ../infinisplat-lab/index.html.
This derivative uses existing SAM 2.1 instance masks to separate surface depths.
A background plate generated with OpenAI's built-in image-generation tool supplies
estimated, previously occluded desk and blind texels on fixed 3D surfaces.
Visible texels in reconstructed surfaces come from the user's source photograph.
This experiment replaces the laptop and cup with fixed opaque triangle surfaces.
Their inferred thickness, cup wall, handle, and unseen materials are approximations.
A fixed source-camera visibility buffer controls photograph projection.
The background PLY excludes the replaced foreground, and the surface and splat
renderers share the depth buffer. Only the cup's local support surface and
background Gaussian colors are adjusted to improve contact and color continuity.
The PLY download contains the background, not the complete hybrid scene.
The complete experiment also requires objects.json and the viewer code/assets.
There is no screen-space photo overlay, crossfade, or depth-of-field concealment.
Generated hidden content is an estimate, not an observation or a measured reconstruction.
This trial covers the main desk at +/-12 degrees, not a complete 180-degree scene.
The original inference timing in scene.json excludes this offline completion stage.
Personal evaluation is registration-exempt; future organizational project use requires PRL registration.
